summary: Extends FoodTracker with a Standards flow: users mark existing food_logs entries as reusable standards, log copies from them on a dedicated Standards page, and manage today's standard-derived entries with aggregated counts and summed nutrition. Includes the schema migration adding standard, source_standard_id, and alcohol_g to foodtracker.food_logs. Adds a three-dots row menu to the Entries page.

classification.why_application: Standard status, copy-from-standard behavior, and aggregated-today display are domain rules specific to FoodTracker's intake model. The decision that a standard is a flag on an existing food_logs row (not a separate entity), the rule that copies always have standard=false, and the delete-most-recent-today semantics are app-specific domain logic that must not be generalised.
non_goals: Using alcohol_g in any UI, calculation, filter, or report in this slice
Quantity editing beyond creating or deleting one row at a time
Editing the nutritional contents of a standard from the Standards page
A separate standards entity or table
Historical backfill of source_standard_id on existing rows
classification.not_platform: The standard flagging model, copy-from-standard insert semantics, and aggregated today view are meaningful only within the FoodTracker intake domain. No general-purpose tagging or template-copying capability should be extracted to platform from this slice.

StandardToggleResult.description: Response for PATCH /api/food/entries/{id}/standard. Confirms the new standard state of the toggled row. Not a Dataset.

fields.id: string — UUID of the updated entry
fields.standard: boolean — the new value of the standard flag after the toggle

StandardsPagePayload.description: Composite response for GET /api/food/standards. Contains two independent collections: all standard dishes (for the bottom section) and today's standard-derived logged rows (for the top section). Not a Dataset — the two-section structure does not fit Dataset naturally. Defined as an explicit named contract per UI_Data_Contract rule 1.

fields.standards: StandardDish[] — all rows where standard=true, ordered by meal_type then dish_name
fields.today_instances: TodayInstance[] — all rows for today where source_standard_id IS NOT NULL, ordered by logged_at DESC

StandardDish.id: string — UUID (this is the source_standard_id consumers pass when logging a copy)
StandardDish.meal_type: string — one of: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack, other

TodayInstance.source_standard_id: string — UUID of the standard dish this row was copied from
TodayInstance.dish_name: string — copied from standard at time of logging
TodayInstance.meal_type: string — copied from standard at time of logging
TodayInstance.count: number (int) — number of logged copies today for this source_standard_id
TodayInstance.total_kcal: number (int) — sum of kcal across all copies today

EntryDetail_Sprint04.description: EntryDetail (from Sprint 03 contracts.named_contracts.EntryDetail) is extended in Sprint 04 to include the two new boolean/UUID fields. All existing fields and serialisation rules remain unchanged. The Sprint 03 contract version is extended, not replaced.

added_fields.standard: boolean — whether this row is marked as a reusable standard
added_fields.source_standard_id: string | null — UUID of the standard this row was copied from, or null

invariants: PATCH /api/food/entries/{id}/standard sets standard to the value in the request body; it does not toggle blindly — the caller supplies the desired state
POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log always sets standard = FALSE on the new row; there is no override path for this rule
POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log always sets source_standard_id = standard_id on the new row
POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log copies nutrition values from the standard row at the time of logging; it does not recompute them
POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log sets logged_at to server datetime.now() (same time source as copy_entry in Sprint 03)

DELETE /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/today-instance deletes exactly one row: the row with source_standard_id = standard_id AND logged_at::date = CURRENT_DATE (server date) ORDER BY logged_at DESC LIMIT 1, identified by its row id. If no matching row exists today, returns HTTP 404.

The standard flag and source_standard_id are independent: a row can have source_standard_id set (it was copied from a standard) and standard=false (it is not itself a standard). These are not mutually exclusive flags.
alcohol_g is persisted in all INSERT and UPDATE operations that write to food_logs (value defaults to 0); it is not returned in any API response in this slice
GET /api/food/standards returns aggregated today_instances computed server-side by GROUP BY source_standard_id; aggregation is not stored
The Entries page row actions remain: the three-dots menu exposes Standard (when standard=false), Remove Standard (when standard=true), and Delete. Delete behavior is unchanged from Sprint 03.
GET /api/food/entries must now include the standard column in rows returned so the frontend can render the correct menu item label
Sprint 03 EntryDetail fields are all preserved; Sprint 04 adds standard (boolean) and source_standard_id (string | null) to the EntryDetail response
failure_modes: NOT_FOUND — requested entry id or standard_id does not exist in foodtracker.food_logs; HTTP 404
NOT_A_STANDARD — POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log called with an id that exists but has standard=false; HTTP 422
NO_TODAY_INSTANCE — DELETE /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/today-instance called when no copy exists today for this standard_id; HTTP 404
VALIDATION_ERROR — PATCH body is not valid JSON or desired_standard is not a boolean; HTTP 422
DB_CONSTRAINT — database CHECK constraint violated at insert or update time; HTTP 400
INTERNAL_ERROR — unexpected exception caught by install_exception_handlers; HTTP 500

consumes: platform_contracts.ColumnSchema, DatasetMeta, Dataset for list responses
provides: HTTP API on port 8012 (container port 8000, host-bound to 127.0.0.1:8012)

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/food/entries/{id}/standard
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Sets the standard flag on an existing food_logs entry to the caller-supplied boolean. Returns a StandardToggleResult confirming the new state. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if entry not found, HTTP 422 if body is invalid.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/standards
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns the two-section Standards page payload: all standard dishes (standard=true rows) and today's aggregated standard-derived logged rows. Aggregation is server-computed by GROUP BY source_standard_id. Not a Dataset — uses StandardsPagePayload named contract.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Creates a new food_logs row by copying nutrition values from the identified standard row. Sets source_standard_id = standard_id, standard = FALSE (firm rule), logged_at = datetime.now(). Returns the new row as an EntryDetail (Sprint 04 v1.1 shape including standard and source_standard_id). Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if standard_id not found, HTTP 422 if the row exists but is not a standard.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/today-instance
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Deletes the single most-recently-logged copy of the given standard for today (WHERE source_standard_id = standard_id AND logged_at::date = CURRENT_DATE ORDER BY logged_at DESC LIMIT 1). Returns HTTP 204. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if no matching instance exists today.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/entries (Sprint 04 change)
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Unchanged endpoint from Sprint 03 except: rows now include the standard (boolean) field so the frontend can render the correct three-dots menu label per row. ENTRIES_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA must add a standard column (type boolean, detail_visible=false, sortable=false).

internal_flow.name: toggle_standard
internal_flow.description: PATCH /api/food/entries/{id}/standard: Parse JSON body, extract desired_standard (boolean, required). Return HTTP 422 if body invalid or desired_standard is not a boolean. SELECT id FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s; return HTTP 404 if not found. UPDATE foodtracker.food_logs SET standard = %s, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = %s. Commit. Return StandardToggleResult {id, standard: desired_standard} as JSON HTTP 200.

internal_flow.name: fetch_standards_page
internal_flow.description: GET /api/food/standards: Execute two queries. Query 1 (standards): SELECT id, meal_type, dish_name, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, good_fat_g, meat_g, red_meat_g, sodium_mg, confidence FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE standard = TRUE ORDER BY meal_type, dish_name. Query 2 (today_instances): SELECT source_standard_id, dish_name, meal_type, COUNT(*) as count, SUM(kcal) as total_kcal, SUM(protein_g) as total_protein_g, SUM(carbs_g) as total_carbs_g, SUM(fat_g) as total_fat_g, SUM(fiber_g) as total_fiber_g, SUM(good_fat_g) as total_good_fat_g, SUM(meat_g) as total_meat_g, SUM(red_meat_g) as total_red_meat_g, SUM(sodium_mg) as total_sodium_mg FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE source_standard_id IS NOT NULL AND logged_at::date = CURRENT_DATE GROUP BY source_standard_id, dish_name, meal_type ORDER BY MAX(logged_at) DESC. Return StandardsPagePayload {standards: [...], today_instances: [...]} as JSON HTTP 200.

internal_flow.name: log_from_standard
internal_flow.description: POST /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/log: SELECT * FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s. Return HTTP 404 if not found. If standard=FALSE on the fetched row, return HTTP 422 (NOT_A_STANDARD). Assign new_id = str(uuid.uuid4()). Set new_logged_at = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'). INSERT into foodtracker.food_logs with all nutrition columns copied from source, new_id as id, new_logged_at as logged_at, standard = FALSE (firm rule — no override), source_standard_id = standard_id, alcohol_g = source['alcohol_g']. RETURNING *. Commit. Return the inserted row serialised as EntryDetail (Sprint 04 v1.1) with HTTP 201.

internal_flow.name: delete_today_instance
internal_flow.description: DELETE /api/food/standards/{standard_id}/today-instance: Execute SELECT id FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE source_standard_id = %s AND logged_at::date = CURRENT_DATE ORDER BY logged_at DESC LIMIT 1. If no row returned, return ApiError HTTP 404 (NO_TODAY_INSTANCE). Execute DELETE FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s using the returned id. Commit. Return HTTP 204 No Content.

internal_flow.name: list_entries_with_standard_flag
internal_flow.description: GET /api/food/entries (Sprint 04 change): Identical to Sprint 03 step 1 except the SELECT now includes the standard column and ENTRIES_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA is extended with a standard column (boolean, sortable=false, detail_visible=false). The row serialiser must include standard: bool(row['standard']).
outputs: Dataset (HTTP 200) with standard field per row | ApiError (HTTP 500)

risks.impact: entries.py adds standard to ENTRIES_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA, _serialise_overview_row, and _serialise_entry_detail. Any mistake in this modification breaks Sprint 03 behavior. Implementer must regression-test GET /api/food/entries and GET /api/food/entries/{id} after the change.

risks.risk: Delete-today-instance targets most-recent row by source_standard_id, not by a UI-supplied row id
risks.impact: If the user has logged two copies of the same standard at almost the same millisecond (e.g. rapid double-tap), the most-recently-logged one is deleted. This is the specified behavior. No row id disambiguation is provided by the client in this slice.

risks.risk: source_standard_id has no foreign key constraint
risks.impact: If a standard row is deleted (via DELETE /api/food/entries/{id} from the Entries page), its source_standard_id references become dangling. today_instances may show aggregated rows with no corresponding entry in the standards list. This is an accepted limitation of the flag-on-row model for this slice.

risks.risk: alcohol_g is stored but not returned in API responses
risks.impact: If a caller reads EntryDetail for a row that has a non-zero alcohol_g, the value is silently omitted. This is correct for this slice. A future slice that adds alcohol_g to the API contract must add it to _serialise_entry_detail and EntryDetail at that time.

risks.risk: standards.py _serialise_standard_log_result is a parallel serialiser to entries.py _serialise_entry_detail
risks.impact: Sprint 04 v1.1 EntryDetail adds standard and source_standard_id. standards.py cannot import the private _serialise_entry_detail from entries.py. It must implement its own serialiser that produces the same shape. If entries.py's serialiser is updated in a future sprint, standards.py must be updated in parallel. This is a documented coupling risk of the no-cross-file-private-access rule.

open_questions.question: When a user deletes a standard row from the Entries page (DELETE /api/food/entries/{id}), should the Standards page update automatically or only on next visit?
open_questions.note: No cross-page state synchronization is defined in this slice. Standards page re-fetches on mount. This is acceptable for a single-user local app.
